page: Amazon Web Services m5dn.2xlarge is a general-purpose, network and EBS-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz, delivering 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU configuration includes a 35 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

For local storage, the m5dn.2xlarge includes a bundled 300 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, offering low-latency local storage. The instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps and is optimized for Elastic Block Store (EBS) performance. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark results indicate average multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 6753.03 and a Passmark CPU score of 7659.89. Memory bandwidth is average, reaching 49.28 GB/sec for large block read-only operations. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 1123.0 and weak single-threaded compression and decompression metrics. Database operations and Redis SET operations perform at average levels, with Redis achieving 6.43 million operations per second. This hardware profile is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, database operations, and software compilation, but exhibits poor performance for larger LLM inference tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services m5dn.2xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with 8 dedicated vCPUs, 4 physical cores, and a 3.1 GHz clock speed. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory and a bundled 300 GB NVMe SSD local instance store. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, this instance delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps and is optimized for EBS. Performance benchmarks show average multi-core CPU capabilities, average memory bandwidth, and average database performance, though single-core performance is weak. It is suitable for balanced workloads such as database operations, software compilation, and general-purpose applications that benefit from local NVMe storage and optimized network throughput. The instance offers a cost-effective balance of compute, memory, and high-speed local storage for resource-dense applications.
